name: Calday
tagline: Simple booking pages, calendars, and reminders for service businesses

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1 service, up to 100 clients, 1 integration and 1 booking page

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited services/clients; unlimited Google, Outlook and iCloud calendars plus Zoom/Meet; payments, add-ons and reminders
tiers.notes: Annual effective rate calculated from the official 20% annual discount.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 service, 100 clients, 1 integration and 1 booking page
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (-20%); 7-day Pro trial, no card; month-to-month cancellation
pricing.hiddenCosts: Stripe's normal payment-processing fees apply, though Calday takes no transaction cut. Existing customers are grandfathered if published prices change.

verdictSummary: Calday's solo core is compact: build a personal booking links tool that reads one calendar, publishes availability, reserves a slot, and writes the event back. A competent builder can reach a useful personal version in one sitting, while the paid product mainly wins on OAuth, calendar reliability.
coreLoopDIY: Build a personal booking links tool that reads one calendar, publishes availability, reserves a slot, and writes the event back.
replacementScope: personal replacement for the core loop
whatYouLose: reliable reminders and timezone edge cases
calendar-provider edge cases and timezone correctness
whyPeopleStillPay: Calday: People pay because a booking tool must never double-book them, leak private events, or send the wrong time to a client.
ongoingBurden: Maintain OAuth, timezone data, webhooks, idempotency, reminders, calendar-provider quirks, and uptime.

priorArt.name: Cal.com
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source scheduling platform and OAuth reference.

alternatives.name: Appointy Free
alternatives.desc: One staffer gets reminders, classes and Square checkout for 100 bookings a month; growth wakes the paywall.

facts.dataFormat: Booking, customer, service and staff records live in Appointy's cloud, with connected calendar and payment data also handled by their respective providers
facts.gapVsPaid: One staff member, five services, 100 monthly appointments and no free two-way calendar sync make it easier to outgrow than Calday.

alternatives.name: Easy!Appointments
alternatives.desc: A proper provider-and-service booking system, provided you will also become its PHP and MySQL caretaker.

facts.install: Upload the release to PHP hosting, create a MySQL database, edit the configuration and run the web installer; Docker is optional
facts.dataFormat: Bookings, providers, services and customers live in MySQL; configuration and logs live on the web server, with optional Google Calendar synchronization
facts.gapVsPaid: It has no managed hosting, built-in payment stack or turnkey SMS service, and the owner must maintain PHP and MySQL.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP and MySQL hosting with database permissions; Google Calendar sync additionally requires a Google Cloud OAuth application

alternatives.name: Setmore Free
alternatives.desc: Four staff, payments, classes and 200 monthly bookings; SMS, recurring appointments and two-way sync cost extra.

facts.dataFormat: Booking, customer and staff records live in Setmore's cloud, with calendar and payment records also passing through connected providers
facts.gapVsPaid: The free plan caps bookings at 200 and excludes recurring appointments, SMS reminders and two-way calendar sync.

alternatives.name: Square Appointments Free
alternatives.desc: A serious free solo booking stack where Square operates; processing fees remain and the feature mix varies by country.

facts.install: Create or use a Square seller account and enable Appointments
facts.dataFormat: Appointment, customer, staff and transaction records live in Square's cloud
facts.gapVsPaid: It is available only in supported Square markets, the free tier is solo and the workflow is tied to Square's payment ecosystem.
facts.setupBlocker: A Square seller account and identity verification, and the service must be available in the user's country

alternatives.name: zcal Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited links and calendars, custom questions, email reminders and Stripe payments; teams are paid and zcal takes 3%.

facts.dataFormat: Account and booking records live in zcal's cloud; Stripe processes and stores payment details for paid bookings
facts.gapVsPaid: It is more meeting-link-oriented and has less provider and service-business administration, while Stripe payments cost an extra 3%.

alternatives.name: Zoho Bookings Free
alternatives.desc: A real one-person booking desk with forms, reminders and two-way sync; staff and payment plumbing cost extra.

facts.dataFormat: Account, booking and customer records live in Zoho's data centres and are synchronized with connected calendar and meeting providers
facts.gapVsPaid: It is limited to one user and one service and does not include payment collection on the free plan.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Picktime Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free plan omits automated reminders, which is one of the small-business basics here.

notes: Strong page because Calday separates a compact personal workflow from the value of long-term polish.
prompt:
Build a usable personal replacement for the core loop of Calday.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a personal booking links tool that reads one calendar, publishes availability, reserves a slot, and writes the event back.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: race-free booking under load; team routing and round robin; reliable reminders and timezone edge cases.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
